key_insight: A symmetry-adapted single-orbital tight-binding model can reproduce the low-energy band structure and spin splitting of chiral 1D hybrid lead-halide perovskites using only a few effective hopping terms.
engineering_relevance: This gives device designers a compact, physics-transparent tool for predicting band-edge electronic, spin, and transport behavior in chiral perovskite optoelectronic and spintronic materials.
method: Built a single-orbital tight-binding Hamiltonian on four symmetry-related sites in the primitive cell.
Included layer, in-plane sublattice, and spin degrees of freedom with separate conduction/valence parameter sets.
Analyzed degeneracies using screw eigenvalues and antiunitary symmetry operators.
evidence_signal: The model was validated against density-functional-theory band dispersions and was reported to quantitatively capture spin splittings and leading spin-polarization patterns near the band edges.
watch_item: The model is tailored to low-energy band-edge physics, so it may not reliably describe higher-energy states or effects beyond the chosen symmetry-adapted term set.
paper_title: Single-orbital tight-binding model for chiral one-dimensional hybrid organic-inorganic lead halide perovskites
